classes.reason: SimpleQuantity and MoneyQuantity are profiles of Quantity (StructureDefinition.derivation constraint), not types. The HL7 validator rejects them as type names: as(SimpleQuantity) fails with 'The type FHIR.SimpleQuantity is not valid', like an invented name (validator_cli 7.0.2, R4, R4B and R5).

R4 MetadataResource is a logical model (StructureDefinition.kind logical): structuredefinition.html says a logical model is not a type an instance has. Decided by the user on 02-11-2026 (ADR-004 D2): excluded, by the specification (fhirpath.html: the FHIR namespace holds primitives, data types and resources; no R4 resource derives from it). validator_cli 7.0.2 accepts as(MetadataResource) but also as(Event) and as(FiveWs), so it measures the name of a non-profile definition, not a type.

R4B hl7.fhir.r4b.core has the abstract type DataType (a specialization with a snapshot, base of the complex types) and gofhir/models r4b does not list it; R5 models does. The validator accepts as(DataType) in R4B.

The paths of an abstract type (Resource.id, DomainResource.text, DataType.id, BackboneType.id, CanonicalResource.name...) are in the snapshot of its StructureDefinition, a specialization. models does not generate them.

models types the nested elements of a data type as BackboneElement. The snapshot gives them Element (Timing.repeat, Dosage.doseAndRate, ElementDefinition.*): the model says timing.repeat.is(BackboneElement), the specification does not.
models gives no ReferenceTargets for the variants of an element with several types (productReference, subjectCanonical...), although each variant keeps the targetProfile of its type.
models gives no ReferenceTargets for CodeableReference elements (R4B and R5), which carry targetProfile like a Reference.
models repeats a target in the list: Media.device is [Device, DeviceMetric, Device] because its snapshot lists Device in two targetProfile; fhirpkg lists each type once.

analyze.reason: fhirpath.Analyze takes 'the model describes Resource.id' as proof that it knows every element of Resource, which only holds for a concrete type. With the elements of the abstract types in the model (as in the snapshots), it rejects contained.contained.empty() (dom-2), issues.issue.severity (bdl-16) and other navigations through a Resource, a DomainResource or a DataType-typed element: 'Resource has no element ...'. The instance is always of a concrete type that can have the element. A defect of fhirpath, not of the model: the model follows the specification and the loss is kept, with its test, until fhirpath fixes it.
